name: bootstrap_confidence_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, large institutional and FII directional orders create persistent 5-second return autocorrelation that lasts 5-15 minutes as TWAP/VWAP algorithms steadily absorb liquidity. A block bootstrap CI (90%) built from the last 120 five-second log returns (10-min window) being entirely above zero means: accounting for the serial correlation structure, the positive directional bias is statistically robust — not a single-bar spike diluted in the average, but a sustained regime. When this condition fires on NIFTY, the same institutional order flow that created the statistical significance still has inventory to deploy, making the next 30-90 seconds of continuation probabilistically favorable. The CI width adapts naturally to current volatility regimes — wide in choppy markets (few signals) and narrow in trending markets (more signals), creating a self-filtering mechanism without explicit regime detection.

indicators.name: log_ret_5s
indicators.purpose: 5-second log return — the raw material for bootstrap resampling. Log returns are additive and better-behaved for statistical inference than simple returns.

indicators.name: block_bootstrap_ci_lower
indicators.formula: 5th percentile of 200 block bootstrap resamples (block_size=6, i.e. 30s blocks) of the mean of the last 120 log returns
indicators.purpose: 120 bars = 10 minutes: same COUNT as original (120 1-min bars) giving equal statistical power, but compressed to 5s so the CI reflects the CURRENT regime rather than 2 hours of stale history. Block size=6 (30s) captures short-run autocorrelation in NIFTY 5-second returns driven by algorithmic order pacing.

indicators.name: block_bootstrap_ci_upper
indicators.purpose: Upper bound of the 90% CI; if this is below zero, statistical evidence for downward directional bias.

conditions: ci_lower > ci_min_signal (entire 90% bootstrap CI above zero, minimum signal 0.8 bps per 5s bar = ~0.1% per 10-min window)
vix_close < vix_cap (default 22; high VIX widens CIs and makes genuine directional signals rarer but noisier)
time_minutes in [570, 920) — after 09:30 warmup, before 15:20 EOD flatten
buy_ce.confirmation: CI entirely positive across 200 bootstrap resamples — no additional confirmation required; the bootstrap test itself is the confirmation

buy_pe.confirmation: CI entirely negative — statistical evidence for bearish directional bias

exit.stop_rationale: Bootstrap signal fires only in statistically high-confidence trending conditions; if NIFTY reverses enough to cost 3 option points (~6 spot pts at ATM delta 0.5), the institutional flow that triggered the signal has reversed and the thesis is broken. At a 30-90s hold, NIFTY typical move is 2-5 option pts — a 3-pt stop catches false breakdowns without being too tight on normal noise.
exit.target_rationale: Sustained institutional momentum on NIFTY typically runs 12-20 spot points before mean reversion; 6 option points (~12 spot pts) captures the first leg of the move, giving a 1:2 risk-reward ratio consistent with the 60%+ win rate expected from bootstrap-filtered entries.

filters.vix_filter: VIX < 22 (high VIX inflates CI width and makes the CI-entirely-positive test harder to pass, paradoxically reducing signal quality)
filters.time_filter: 09:30-15:20 IST — 09:30 ensures 10 min of warm-up bars for bootstrap window
filters.volume_filter: None — applied to NIFTY index; volume is available but not used as CI test subsumes regime detection
filters.trend_filter: None — CI test inherently captures the trend direction; no separate trend filter needed
filters.spread_filter: None — limit order execution at close prices, no bid-ask spread cost

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low-to-medium — bootstrap inference for short-horizon direction prediction is novel at 5s frequency; however, if market becomes more autocorrelated (or less), CI thresholds need re-calibration

adaptation_notes: Original strategy applied bootstrap CI to 120 1-minute returns on NIFTY50 stocks (2-hour lookback). Converted to 120 five-second returns on NIFTY index (10-minute lookback) for three reasons: (1) same count = same statistical power; (2) 5s bars make the CI reflect the current intraday regime rather than stale 2-hour history; (3) index is smoother than individual stocks, reducing noise in the bootstrap samples. Session start moved from 11:15 (original needed 120 1-min bars from open) to 09:30 (10-min warmup). Hold time compressed from 15-45 min to 30-90s; stop/target calibrated to NIFTY ATM option premium moves at that timescale. Bootstrap reps reduced to 200 (from original's 500) as 200 gives stable 5th/95th percentiles for 120-sample windows.
weaknesses: Block bootstrap with block_size=6 (30s blocks) assumes autocorrelation decays within 30s — if NIFTY has longer-run micro-trends (e.g., 2-3 minute momentum cycles), CI width may be underestimated
Running 200 bootstrap resamples per bar in Python is the compute bottleneck; full session backtest takes ~15-20s per day — acceptable for research, but limits parameter sweep granularity
CI-entirely-above-zero is strict: in choppy markets, this rarely fires, leading to zero-trade days — position sizing needs to account for low trade frequency
Signal fires after the move has already started (CI reflects the past 10 min); in fast-reversing intraday NIFTY regimes, entry may occur near the end of the move rather than the beginning
